subject: Pilot scope & cost playback — ClearPath inference economics
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Theo Martin <theo.martin@clearpath.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 17:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot scope & cost playback — ClearPath inference economics

Hi Theo — great to meet earlier. Wanted to capture a short playback from today's call so we have shared alignment on priorities and next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain / goals (what you told us)
- Primary pain: per-inference unit cost rising as your transaction volume scales (esp. peak checkout flows).
- Current throughput target: 150 req/s at p95 latency < 200ms for short-form responses (~128 tokens).
- Constraints: strict PII handling for payment flows (no external caching of raw payloads), and preference to stay on economies that minimize GPU-hours.

Current stack
- Model: running a Mixture-of-Experts derivative on dedicated G4 fleet (self-hosted).
- Orchestration: internal autoscaler + SQS-based queuing.
- Observability: homegrown traces + Datadog; not currently instrumented for KV cache hit rates or batching breakdown.

Success criteria for pilot (what would make this successful)
1) 30–40% reduction in per-inference cost (tokens or GPU-hour normalized) without regression in accuracy on the checkout intent set.
2) Maintain p95 < 250ms at pilot traffic.
3) Clear playbook for safe rollout (canary + rollback hooks) and a security checklist for PII handling.

Redwood's proposed pilot approach (high level)
- Quick modelling: run a 2-week pilot on Redwood Dedicated with a batching+KV cache config tuned to your latency envelope.
- Two model variants: a cost-optimized quantized variant and a high-accuracy variant for fallbacks.
- Track: tokens-per-call, GPU-hours, cache hit rates, p95 latency, and accuracy against your test set.

Open questions we asked you to confirm
- Will you be able to provide a short labeled prompt set (50–100 examples) for quality validation?
- Are there any regulatory constraints preventing even transient prefix caching for masked fields?
- Who on your side owns procurement for dedicated capacity (timing of contract)?

Attachments: I attached a one-pager pilot scope and a rough cost export from today's numbers.

Next steps (agreed on the call)
1) ClearPath to share labeled prompt set + traffic profile (Theo, Lina) — by Thu 21 Jan.
2) Redwood to send a focused pilot SOW and a cost estimate (Ava + Aditya) — by Wed 20 Jan.
3) Quick architecture review call with your infra lead to discuss KV caching and data masking (Monica to set up) — week of Jan 25.

Thanks again — we can be flexible on pilot duration if you need more time to route procurement.

Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pilot scope & cost playback — ClearPath inference economics

Ava — thanks for the clear summary, that matches our notes. A few clarifications: 

- Labeled prompts: yes, we can deliver ~75 examples. I'll have Lina pull those together and include the current scoring rubric.
- Data masking: we cannot persist full payloads outside our VPC; however, we can provide masked prefixes and agree to a short-lived KV cache if keys are scrubbed and logged. Need to confirm with security.
- Procurement: procurement is handled by our vendor team; they will want an enterprise SOW and an estimated monthly run-rate. We're aiming for a Feb window to start procurement conversations.

One ask: can Redwood provide a simple template that shows unit cost sensitivity (batch sizes 1/4/16, plus a quantized vs fp16 column)? That will help the vendor team.

—Theo
Theo Martin
Head of AI Platforms, ClearPath Labs

Theo / Ava — looping in procurement signal and a quick note on what we typically provide.

- We'll include a cost sensitivity table (batch sizes: 1, 4, 16; quantization: fp16, int8-ish trial) in the SOW. It will show token-level cost and GPU-hour projections at your traffic profile.
- For the security ask: short-lived KV caching (TTL < 60s) with scrubbed keys + audit logs is an approach we've used with other payment customers. We'll document the exact masking expectations in the security checklist.
- I'll draft a one-page Excel that Lina can pass to procurement; Ava, will send the SOW draft with that workbook attached.
